successors.name: British Colonial Empire
successors.text: Berbice, merged on 21 July 1831 with Demerara-Essequibo into British Guiana

ledger.x: 1627: Abraham van Peere settles Berbice under the West India Company's suzerainty ('Berbice was settled in 1627 by the businessman Abraham van Peere').
1678: a charter makes Berbice 'a hereditary fief of the Dutch West India Company, in the possession of the Van Peere family'.
1712 (November): 'Berbice was briefly occupied by the French' under Jacques Cassard.
1714 (24 October): Van Peere's relatives and associates paid the ransom 'thereby acquiring the colony'; the French leave.
1720 (24 October): five owners found the Society of Berbice, a public company on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange (infobox: 24 October 1720 to 1821).
1781 (27 February): 'British forces occupied Berbice' in the Fourth Anglo-Dutch War.
1782 (January): 'the colonies were recaptured by the French' (infobox: 22 January 1782).
1782 (January): the French hold Berbice until the Treaty of Paris.
1783: 'The Treaty of Paris (1783) restored Dutch rule.'
1792 (1 January): Berbice becomes a Dutch state colony.
1796 (22 April): 'The colony was on 22 April 1796 again captured by Britain, however this time without a fight.'
1802 (27 March): 'until 27 March 1802, when Berbice was restored to the Batavian Republic' under the Treaty of Amiens.
1803 (September): 'the British occupied the territory again, this time for good.'
1814: under the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 the colony was 'formally ceded to the United Kingdom'; the Netherlands ratified it on 20 November 1815.

wars.name: Fourth Anglo-Dutch War and French Revolutionary Wars in Berbice
wars.outcome: British occupation from 27 February 1781, the French from January 1782 to the 1783 Treaty of Paris, British again from 22 April 1796 to 27 March 1802, and permanently from September 1803.

certainty.note: A river colony on the Berbice and Canje; the page gives no frontier or area, and the boundary with Essequibo-Demerara is not on it.
